profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Minneapolis - Chaska) is located at 3500 Lyman Blvd, Chaska, MN 55318. The operator publishes a footprint of 160,838 square feet and 9 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18, HITRUST. Xcel Energy, Minnesota's dominant utility, has acknowledged that data center growth is pushing it to extend natural gas plant operations into the 2030s despite the state's clean-energy commitments; Minnesota division president Ryan Long said the utility "may have been looking to extend some gas (contracts) on our system to get us through a portion of the 2030s," even as Xcel committed $45 billion in infrastructure investment over five years, per Data Center Dynamics' reporting. As of late 2023 Xcel reported 60 megawatts of existing Minnesota data center load with 15 more under construction, and a Meta agreement starting at 10 megawatts and expanding to 75 megawatts within a decade. Minnesota's 2023 clean-electricity law mandates 100% carbon-free power delivery by 2040, a target a state deputy commerce commissioner has said may be difficult to meet given the pace of data center demand; the state's current generation mix is about 33% renewables, 24% natural gas, and 21% nuclear. Minneapolis's city council separately approved a six-month moratorium on new data center permits, with downtown facilities exempted, reflecting rising local scrutiny of the sector's power and land-use footprint even as some officials weigh downtown data centers as a tax-base tool.

Chaska already hosted three operating data centers as of 2025, including one that sold in an all-cash transaction for $31 million in 2024, and a new entrant, Washington D.C.-based CloudHQ, has secured site control and preliminary city approvals for a 1.4-million-square-foot campus on 70 acres north of Engler Boulevard, according to Finance & Commerce reporting. A key draw for data center operators has been Chaska City Electric, the city's municipal utility, which offers lower and more predictable rates than the region's investor-owned utilities, a reliability and cost advantage relevant to power-intensive colocation buildings like this one. The same industrial corridor has drawn adjacent large-footprint development, including a 240,000-square-foot EDCO Manufacturing facility on former farmland just south of the CloudHQ site and a 148,000-square-foot Beckman Coulter expansion approved in December 2024.

reading.body:
At 9 MW across 160,838 square feet, Flexential Minneapolis - Chaska can support either roughly 225 AI training racks at 40 kW each or roughly 900 colocation racks at 10 kW each, but the operator publishes no breakdown of actual tenant workloads or power allocation.

The facility holds seven compliance certifications that qualify it for regulated tenants: SOC audits for financial and operational controls, PCI DSS for payment card processors, ITAR for defense and aerospace data, NIST 800-53 for federal security, and HITRUST for healthcare. These certifications signal what workloads the building is built to contain, not what occupies it. No tenant names are published.

Among thirteen mapped Minnesota data centers, Chaska ranks first by published IT capacity. That ranking is an artifact of disclosure: twelve other facilities in the state publish no capacity figures at all, so their true scale is unknown. One operator's willingness to publish megawatts does not confirm Chaska's physical dominance in the region, only that most operators do not disclose this data.
